title: Genomic insights into high‐sugar tolerance and probiotic properties of Pediococcus pentosaceus MP13, a potential probiotic isolated from traditional fermented rose jam
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

Pediococcus pentosaceus MP13 was previously isolated from traditionally fermented rose jam, a high-sugar fermentation environment. This strain exhibits promising fermentation and probiotic-related properties, but the genomic features potentially associated with its tolerance to high-sugar conditions remain unclear. This study evaluated the effects of sugar stress, selected probiotic properties, and characterized genomic features of MP13.

RESULTS

Increasing sugar concentrations inhibited MP13 growth and increased extracellular conductivity and nucleic acid leakage, both approaching plateaus at higher concentrations, while cells exposed to 55% sugar retained relatively intact coccoid morphology. MP13 also showed appreciable cell surface hydrophobicity, approximately 75% auto-aggregation, and inhibitory activity against the tested indicator bacteria. Its complete genome comprised a single 1 939 576 bp circular chromosome with a GC content of 38.46%. Comparative genomic analysis showed high overall similarity to related P. pentosaceus strains, while revealing inter-strain genomic variation. MP13 utilized 22 of 49 tested carbohydrates, and genome annotation identified diverse carbohydrate metabolism-related pathways, 212 putative CAZyme genes, and 33 substrate-specific PTS genes, suggesting broad genetic potential for carbohydrate metabolism despite phenotype–genotype discrepancies for sucrose and d-melibiose. Functional annotation identified genes with predicted roles in osmotic, acid, and bile stress responses, and adhesion, while genome mining revealed putative bacteriocin-associated loci. Safety assessment showed a non-hemolytic phenotype and no known toxin or biogenic amine biosynthesis genes, while no corresponding known acquired antimicrobial resistance genes determinants were detected for previously reported resistance to gentamicin, erythromycin, and penicillin.

CONCLUSION

The phenotypic and genomic characteristics of P. pentosaceus MP13 support its further evaluation for sugar-rich food fermentation and as a probiotic candidate. Carbohydrate metabolism- and stress-response-related genomic features suggest potential contributions to high-sugar tolerance, but their functional roles require expression- and function-based validation. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
